title: release.yml's breaking-bump gate is already red: CHANGELOG 0.11.0 carries the legacy BEHAVIOUR CHANGE marker the checker refuses
description:
Found while running gates for LCLI-648 (2026-09-29), and measured to be PRE-EXISTING rather than caused by it: `node scripts/check-breaking-bump.mjs` on a clean dev tree returns the same failure.

WHAT FAILS. The script reports: "The version bump does not match the CHANGELOGs (lore read 28 sections; quest read 11 sections from opum-ai/quest-cli@dev:CHANGELOG.md): - lore: ## [0.11.0] - 2026-09-27 carries lore legacy **BEHAVIOUR CHANGE:** marker; use a `### Changed (breaking)` heading instead (the canonical spelling, per quest-cli QCLI-328)". The offending bullet is CHANGELOG.md:422, inside the shipped 0.11.0 section.

WHY IT MATTERS. The checker runs only from the release path (.github/workflows/release.yml:209,222), so nothing on a PR or on dev turns red for it -- the next release does, at the one moment nobody can iterate on it cheaply. That is the failure shape this repository profile names explicitly: a gate that is wrong fails only during a release.

THE TENSION THE FIX HAS TO SETTLE, and it is a real one rather than a formatting nit. The 0.11.0 section is RELEASED HISTORY, and the fleet rule is that history is not rewritten -- a Done record is not edited to remove a word. But the checker refuses the legacy spelling at any bump level. So either the released section is converted to the canonical heading form (a formatting change to a shipped entry, which the canonical-form argument supports since the heading is what the tool reads), or the checker is taught to scope its legacy-marker refusal to unreleased sections. Which side gives way is a small decision with a durable consequence and should be recorded rather than picked in passing.

NOT FIXED IN LCLI-648: that task is the Bun pin, and this predates it by two days. Filed rather than absorbed, per the same rule the pin task itself was filed under.

acceptanceCriteria.text: node scripts/check-breaking-bump.mjs exits 0 on dev, verified by running it, so the release path no longer fails for a reason that predates the release being cut

The record states which side gave way -- the released 0.11.0 sections marker converted to the canonical heading form, or the checker scoped to unreleased sections -- with the reasoning, since one of the two is history and this repository does not rewrite history by accident
The fix does not silently rewrite the 0.11.0 entries prose: only the marker form changes, and the diff shows nothing else

plan: 1. Measure both checker invocations and release.yml's actual one (--quest-ref main, no --next) to scope which red is real.

2. Convert the 0.11.0 legacy **BEHAVIOUR CHANGE:** marker to the canonical '### Changed (breaking)' heading form; prose untouched; the sibling non-breaking Changed bullet gets its own '### Changed' heading.
3. Update the LCLI-632 test that pins the real CHANGELOG's stale-window red to the new canonical bytes; record which side gave way and why on the task.
4. Gates: node scripts/check-breaking-bump.mjs exits 0; bun test and bun run lore check on the pinned runtime; PR into dev.
implementationNotes: DECISION (AC2): the released section gave way, converted to the canonical form; the checker's rule is unchanged. Reasoning: (1) the ruling that refuses the legacy marker postdates the entry -- 0.11.0 shipped 2026-09-27, the any-bump-level refusal was ruled 2026-09-28 (recorded on LCLI-632) -- so the red is a new rule applied retroactively to shipped bytes, and the only remedy the message names (rewrite the marker) is unavailable for a section nobody re-authors. (2) CHANGELOG.md is NOT in the npm tarball (package.json files: bin, README.md, LICENSE), so editing it diverges from no published artifact; it is a repository document. (3) The canonical form states the same fact in the form the repo already uses in adjacent sections (Unreleased carries '### Changed (breaking)'; an earlier released section does too), so the entry is re-spelled, not falsified -- no prose word changed. (4) The alternative -- scoping the checker's legacy refusal to sections the author can still edit -- narrows a ruled gate, diverges further from quest-cli's mirror, and needs a reviewer pass on scripts/; it is the better choice only if the ruling itself is being revisited, which this task is not. DIFF: CHANGELOG.md 0.11.0 gains '### Changed (breaking)' above the LCLI-606 entry with the bold marker stripped, and the non-breaking LCLI-596 bullet gets its own '### Changed' heading; nothing else. MEASURED: node scripts/check-breaking-bump.mjs exits 0 (was exit 1 naming **BEHAVIOUR CHANGE:**); --next 0.12.0 already exited 0 before and still does; release.yml's actual invocation (--quest-ref main, no --next) checks the version's OWN section at the dispatched commit, so the 0.11.0 marker never red the 0.12.0 dispatch -- what it red was any no-flag run on lore's bytes (local gate runs, and a rehearsal dispatch from a ref whose package.json still names 0.11.0), correcting the task description's 'the next release does' to the measured object. TESTS: test/lcli632-breaking-bump-gate.test.ts's real-CHANGELOG case now asserts the released section reads breaking=true, legacyMarker=false, no problems (not merely the absence of a refusal); the AC2 synthetic refusals are unchanged and still pass. GATES: bun test 4810 pass / 0 fail / 1 skip (pinned runtime); bun run lore check exit 0; breaking-bump exit 0.
